notes: REPLACES AN AMOSTOOLS STUB. Until 2026-08-12 this row held only the token table with the library stripped out from under it -- both length fields zero, no code, every routine word overwritten with `====` -- so the tier could not rise above `manual`. The real library's table is IDENTICAL to the stub's, entry for entry, id for id and spec for spec, which is a check on the AMOSTools reader as much as on this registration. What changes is that the code is now here to read. THE LIBRARY IS CALLED `SBASE_EX` -- not a .lib, and not named for the product. The archive's own Installer script settles it: `(set #libname "SBASE_EX")` then `(set #newlibname "AmosPro_SymBase.Lib")`, so the file is renamed on the way in. It was found by its token table, which opens `db se`, `db us`, `db addres`, `db clos` with the high bit on each name's last character as AMOS stores them. DBENCH AND SYMBASE ARE THE SAME PRODUCT AT TWO AGES, both by Lázár Zoltán. dbench-0.42's 23 named keywords are symbase-0.94's first 23 in the same order, and all but the last two at the same ids -- `db sel`, `db use`, `db address`, `db close`, `db flen`, `db fieldno`, `db saved on`, `db saved off` and on. Neither should be ported without the other open. SymBase 0.92's readme records a keyword REMOVAL -- "REM: Date functions removed to a separate extension / No more needs date.library" -- which is exactly the shape that makes one build's tokens detokenise to nonsense under another, so the `renumbered` verdict may apply across the family and has not been checked. FOUR VERSIONS ARE HELD and the earlier three are what make the renumbering question answerable: 0.58 is a third the size of 0.85, so something large changed between them. The stub collection had all four token tables; the real 0.94 binary is the one registered.  ALSO IN THE ARCHIVE: Comp/SymBase/Tools/ -- Create, Dedit, DSort, Index, Server and Client, all compiled AMOS programs, with Examples/BOOKSHELF and its source. `Libs/gui.library` (46,948 bytes) is there because the tools need it; that is the GUI family's back-end, not SymBase's, and it is the first copy of it in the corpus. THE GUIDE WAS MISSED when this row was registered and it changes what a port has to work with: `Comp/SymBase/Docs/SymBase.guide` is 35,603 bytes and 47 nodes, about thirty of them one per keyword, and three of them -- `Dbhead`, `BANK` and `Index_head` -- document the on-disk and in-bank structures field by field. Most of it is in Hungarian, including every format table. Its header still reads `@$VER 0.85` while its body says "System last updated: 2005.04.19.", so it is the 0.94 guide with a stale version line. WHAT SYMBASE IS: an xBase engine, and the guide says so -- "the used database file is Xbase compatible". The keywords are dBase III's, name for name: `Db Use`, `Db Select`, `Db Skip`, `Db Locate`, `Db Pack`, `Db Zap`, `Db Append`, `Db Recall`, `Db Setdeleted On`, `Db Found`, `Db Order`, `Db Sort`, `Db Alias`. That is why the library is only 5,560 bytes: the format carries the design. AND THERE IS AN ARTIFACT TO CHECK A PORT AGAINST. `Comp/SymBase/Examples/Book.dbf` parses exactly as the `Dbhead` node describes -- id $03, 24 records of 130 bytes, header 194, five fields (title, otitle and author C40, year N5, kind N4, which sum to 129 plus the deleted flag), the $0d field terminator at 192 and the $1a at 3314 where the header says the data ends. The file is 3,786 bytes, so 472 of trailing slack sit past that $1a: the HEADER is authoritative and a reader trusting the file length would invent three and a half records. The Server and Client tools talk over an AREXX port rather than a socket -- "Standalone database server, which works via an arexx port" -- and they are separate programs, not part of the extension. THE TWO TABLES ARE NOT ID-COMPATIBLE, and this is the `renumbered` case the sweep exists to catch. DBench's 23 named entries are SymBase's first 22 at identical ids and then diverge: id $0166 is DBench's `db goto` and SymBase's `db get`, and $0174 is DBench's `db put` and SymBase's `db getf`. 0.94 inserted `Db Get` and `Db Getf` there and pushed `Db Goto` out to $0182 and `Db Put$` to $0190. So a DBench program's `Db Goto n` read against SymBase's table detokenises as `Db Get`, which is a FUNCTION with spec `00` where `db goto` is an instruction with `I0` -- it does not merely do the wrong thing, it will not parse. Binding the right identity is what keeps the two apart, and dispatch is by NAME, so one port serves both. BOTH CLAIM SLOT 21 AND THE BINARIES SAY SO: DBench routine 0 is `move.l a3,$238(a5) / moveq #$14,d0` and SymBase's is the same store, and ($238-$f8)/16+1 is 21 on the ExtAdr layout (+Equ.s:1185). They cannot be loaded together, which is what successive builds of one product are supposed to do.
